subject: Urgent: NovaRetail VPC backpressure & 503 surge — exec sync + proposed tuning
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novaretail.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 503s and request to pause new traffic

Hi Ava / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 503 responses from the NovaRetail VPC deployment at ~07:50 PDT. P95 latency also climbed from ~220ms to ~1.3s in a 10-minute window and our customer-facing checkout flows reported intermittent failures. Error rate peaked at ~6.2% for a 5-minute bucket.

We have temporarily paused non-critical traffic on our side but the checkout path (primary) still hits the service. Can the Redwood team please:
- confirm if there is an ongoing platform-level throttling/backpressure event;
- provide immediate mitigation steps (canary rollback, config tweak, or emergency routing) we can take in parallel;
- share any ETA for stabilization.

I've attached a short telemetry extract (nova-telemetry-agg.csv) and will forward full svc debug bundle if helpful. This is causing customer complaints and a partial outage for one of our regions — execs are asking for an update.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
VP Product, NovaRetail

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 09:05 AM, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com wrote:

I've pulled the first set of node-level stats from NovaRetail's VPC:
- Ingestion queue depth spiked from median 12 -> 268 over ~6 minutes;
- p95 CPU on the inference workers rose to ~94% and GPU utilization shows frequent tq stalls;
- We observed a backlog of KV cache miss storms correlated with new long-context chat requests hitting the private cluster;
- Several workers reported repeated 503s with an internal error code "COLD_KV_TIMEOUT".

Immediate recommendations (start in next 10–15min):
- Apply an ingress token-based rate cap at the VPC edge to smooth bursts (reduce peak QPS by ~30%).
- Temporarily switch the checkout route to the earlier model variant (v1.14-q4) that has smaller KV working set; this should cut memory pressure and reduce miss storms.
- Perform a rolling restart of the three highest-queue pods (order: pod-7, pod-3, pod-9) with 60s stagger to clear pathological heap growth.

I've uploaded a trimmed debug archive (svc-debug-20270403.tar.gz) to the shared Drive link (INF-1428). If ingress can't be throttled from your side, we can apply a temporary firewall rule at the VPC egress to edgeops@edgeopt.com (they manage your CDN) — will need a quick thumbs-up from NovaRetail.

Vivek
Head of Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

Please send the exact CLI for rolling restart and the model rollback command so our infra team can run in parallel to your ops team. Execs want an ETA for stabilization.

Date: 2027-04-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final update: NovaRetail VPC incident — cause, mitigation, next steps

Sofia / Carlos — final summary after post-mortem triage: 
Root cause (summary):
- A client-side rollout increased median context length for a large fraction of requests; that drove a spike in KV cache working set and cache-miss storms in the private VPC. Miss storms caused head-of-line blocking and inflated worker memory/CPU, which led to COLD_KV_TIMEOUT errors and 503s.

Mitigation applied during incident (timeline):
- 09:25 PDT: NovaRetail applied CDN ingress throttling via edgeopt (reduced peak QPS by ~28%).
- 09:30 PDT: We rolled checkout route to model v1.14-q4 (shorter KV footprint).
- 09:34–09:46 PDT: Rolling restart of pods pod-7, pod-3, pod-9 completed.
- 09:50 PDT: Error rate dropped <0.3% and p95 returned to ~230ms.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Long-term mitigation: implement client-side context-length caps and add server-side admission control to prevent KV-miss storms (owner: NovaRetail infra).
2) Redwood action: schedule a quantization/profile review and re-evaluate cache sizing for NovaRetail's workload (owner: Vivek) — deliverable: tuning playbook and recommended cache config by 2027-04-08.
3) Joint runbook update: add a fast rollback path for model variants and an automated ingress-smoothing policy (owner: Monica + NovaRetail SRE).

Exec ask: Marcus / Laura, please prepare a 2-line note for NovaRetail execs confirming impact and remediation. I recommend offering two hours of credit for the checkout downtime window while we complete the runbook updates (we can discuss discount mechanics offline).

If you want, I'll set up a 30-minute post-mortem with NovaRetail tech + execs tomorrow to walk through the playbook.

Thanks all for the quick coordination — big win getting checkout stabilized.

- Ava
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
